title: Quant-path timeline compressor and lazy dequant elision for streaming prefill
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: In streaming prefill and decode workloads we pay repeated dequantization costs when model execution hops between INT8/FP8 fast paths and fallback FP32 kernels. For low-latency short-turn interactions (chatty traffic) the dequant overhead dominates tail latency and increases CPU/GPU memory traffic, eroding cost benefits of quantization.

Goal: Implement a runtime-level 'timeline compressor' that coalesces contiguous token execution segments with identical precision semantics and enables lazy dequant elision where safe. The feature should: (1) minimize the number of dequant operations during prefill and streaming decode, (2) allow mixed-precision kernels to run without eager conversion when downstream ops can consume quantized tensors, and (3) expose a small set of heuristics and telemetry to the scheduler to make precision-handoff decisions per-request.

Scope: This ticket covers design, a prototype kernel adapter, scheduler hooks for timeline compression, microbenchmarks, and a single-model canary (redwood/gpt-medium-quant) in staging. Integration with full KV cache eviction heuristics and global batching policies will be subsequent tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Prefill + decode end-to-end for redwood/gpt-medium-quant shows >=15% tail latency reduction (p95) compared to baseline with identical throughput
Total dequant kernel invocations reduced by >=40% in representative chatty workload trace (internal trace set 'chat-20k')
No quality regressions on prompt-based unit tests and eval set (logprob drift < 0.1 on calibrated prompts)
Canary deployable in staging with flag runtime.enable_timeline_compression=true and opt-in per-model configuration

design_decisions: We will represent precision spans as lightweight metadata attached to KV-cache segments to avoid annotating every tensor in the hot path.
Lazy dequant will be allowed only when the downstream kernel advertises 'quant-tolerant' consumption semantics via a new kernel capability bit.
To preserve determinism we will not allow lazy dequant across model boundary ops (e.g., logits->sampling); such boundaries will force a deterministic materialization.

Default heuristic: if a precision span length >= 4 tokens OR predicted downstream arithmetic intensity > threshold, perform eager dequant; otherwise, enable lazy elision to prioritize latency. Heuristic tunables will be model-configurable.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Lazy dequant may expose hidden numerical differences for some ops (softmax scaling). Mitigation: run targeted numeric regression tests and add per-op opt-out flags.
Tradeoff: Storing span metadata increases memory metadata overhead slightly; chosen representation is compressed and amortized across KV entries.
Risk: Interaction with global batching may reduce opportunities for compression; scheduler will attempt per-batch coalescing and fall back gracefully.
Tradeoff: Complexity added to kernel interface (capabilities bit) vs benefit in kernel invocation reduction. We'll gate on empirically measured wins before enabling by default.
notes_and_experiment_results: Initial microbenchmark (single-GPU A100): baseline decode p95 38ms -> prototype timeline compressor p95 30ms (-21%).
Dequant invocations dropped by 48% in the prototype run using chat-20k trace; memory bandwidth decreased by ~12%.
Observed a rare numeric delta in temperature-sensitive sampling test; tracked to FP32 accumulation in a custom op. Added per-op opt-out and re-ran with no quality regression.
